question: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 120° and a radius of 7 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of (2pi)/(3) radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the central angle of the second sector from radians to degrees to easily compare them.

Angle in degrees = (2π ÷ 3) × (180° ÷ π) = 120°.

Both sectors belong to the same circle (radius = 7 cm) and have equal central angles of 120°.

Since both the radius and the central angles are identical, their areas must be exactly equal.

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 7 cm

Central angle of the first sector (θ₁) = 120°

Central angle of the second sector (θ₂) = 2π/3 radians

**Formulas Used:**

Area of sector (degrees) = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Area of sector (radians) = (1 ÷ 2) × θ × r²

**Calculations:**

Calculating the area of the first sector (A₁):

⇒ A₁ = (120° ÷ 360°) × π × (7)²

⇒ A₁ = (1 ÷ 3) × 49π

⇒ A₁ = 49π ÷ 3 cm²

Calculating the area of the second sector (A₂):

⇒ A₂ = (1 ÷ 2) × (2π ÷ 3) × (7)²

⇒ A₂ = (π ÷ 3) × 49

⇒ A₂ = 49π ÷ 3 cm²

Finding the ratio of their areas:

⇒ A₁ : A₂ = (49π ÷ 3) : (49π ÷ 3)

⇒ A₁ : A₂ = 1 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1:1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector is directly proportional to its central angle. It represents a specific fraction of the entire area of the circle. Formula: Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr²

Radians and Degrees

Degrees and radians are two distinct units for measuring angles. A complete circle equals 360° or 2π radians. Conversion: Angle in Degrees = Angle in Radians × (180° ÷ π).

Arc Length

The length of the boundary arc of a sector relies on the central angle. The formula is: L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr (when in degrees) or simply L = rθ (when in radians).
